defaults.permitted_development: A more-than-one-storey extension can be permitted development in Wales only in tighter cases, mainly at the rear or side, where it stays behind the principal elevation and clears the boundary-distance tests.

rules.height_rules: No part should exceed the height of the existing roof, and eaves should not exceed the existing eaves. Where any part within 2m of a boundary has eaves over 3m, the work is not permitted development.
rules.depth_rules: A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor. A side extension with more than one storey must be set back at least 1m from the principal elevation and the resulting house must be no more than 50% wider than the original.
rules.boundary_rules: Upper floors to a rear extension must be at least 10.5m from the rear boundary. More-than-one-storey side extensions must be at least 10.5m from the opposite side boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Do not place a more-than-one-storey extension forward of the principal elevation. Side extensions also remain restricted near highways, and the roof pitch should match the existing dwellinghouse as far as practicable.
rules.materials_rules: External wall and roof materials should match the existing house as closely as practicable.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls in Wales narrow these rights. Side extensions on designated land are more restricted, two-storey side extensions are not permitted there, and Article 4 directions can remove further rights.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually needed for works affecting character, and planning permission may also be required.

rules.permitted_development: The Welsh two-storey route is narrow. A more-than-one-storey extension only stays within permitted development where it satisfies the rear or side limits, remains behind the principal elevation and meets the 10.5m boundary tests.

rules.height_rules: Keep the extension below the existing roof height and do not lift the eaves above the existing eaves. Near the boundary, eaves above 3m will take the work out of the Welsh PD route.
rules.depth_rules: A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor. A side extension with more than one storey must be set back at least 1m from the principal elevation and the resulting house must be no more than 50% wider than the original.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary distance is central to the Welsh two-storey route. Rear upper floors need 10.5m to the rear boundary, and upper floors in side extensions need 10.5m to the opposite side boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Do not place a more-than-one-storey extension forward of the principal elevation. Side extensions also remain restricted near highways, and the roof pitch should match the existing dwellinghouse as far as practicable.
rules.materials_rules: Match new wall and roof finishes closely to the existing house so the upper floor reads as part of the dwelling rather than a later stack-on.

rules.depth_rules: A rear extension with more than one storey can project up to 4m at ground floor and up to 3m above ground floor. A side extension with more than one storey must be set back at least 1m from the principal elevation and the resulting house must be no more than 50% wider than the original.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary distance is central to the Welsh two-storey route. Rear upper floors need 10.5m to the rear boundary, and upper floors in side extensions need 10.5m to the opposite side boundary.
rules.roof_rules: Do not place a more-than-one-storey extension forward of the principal elevation. Side extensions also remain restricted near highways, and the roof pitch should match the existing dwellinghouse as far as practicable.
rules.materials_rules: Match new wall and roof finishes closely to the existing house so the upper floor reads as part of the dwelling rather than a later stack-on.

restrictions.conservation_area: Protected-area controls in Wales narrow these rights. Side extensions on designated land are more restricted, two-storey side extensions are not permitted there, and Article 4 directions can remove further rights.
restrictions.listed_building: Do not rely on standard householder permitted development rights for a listed building. Listed building consent is usually needed for works affecting character, and planning permission may also be required.
